stories.title: Rising yields rattle stocks, but CNBC still likes its AI and retail picks
stories.summary: Bond yields rose this week and put pressure on the broader stock market. CNBC's markets team says it still favors its top AI and retail stock picks despite the pressure. The piece treats the yield move as a near-term risk, not a reason to sell those positions.
stories.whyItMatters: Higher yields raise the discount rate on future earnings. That hits richly valued AI and retail stocks the hardest.
whatToWatch: Further moves in bond yields
Whether CNBC's picks hold up if yields keep rising
questions: What is driving yields higher right now?
How much further could yields climb?

stories.title: Nvidia customers reportedly face 15%+ server price hikes as memory costs soar
stories.summary: Nvidia's customers have reportedly been warned of server price increases of more than 15%. Rising memory chip costs are the cause, according to reports from CNBC and Investing.com. Both outlets say the warning has already reached buyers of AI servers.
stories.whyItMatters: Higher server costs raise the price of building AI infrastructure. That is a key cost input for the AI spending boom.
whatToWatch: Memory chip price trends
Comments from hyperscalers on AI infrastructure costs
Nvidia's next earnings report
questions: Which memory makers gain the most from this?
Will cloud providers pass the higher costs to customers?

stories.title: Russia stocks close lower as MOEX index holds steady
stories.summary: Russian stocks closed lower on the day. The MOEX Russia Index itself ended little changed, Investing.com reported. No further detail on sector moves was given.
stories.whyItMatters: The move offers a small data point for readers tracking sanctions-hit and emerging markets.
whatToWatch: The next session's move in the MOEX index
questions: What drove the gap between falling stocks and a flat index?

stories.title: Canada announces retaliatory tariffs on US goods as trade talks collapse
stories.summary: Canada said it will impose retaliatory tariffs on US goods. The move follows the breakdown of trade talks between the two countries, MarketWatch reported.
stories.whyItMatters: New tariffs raise costs for companies that trade across the US-Canada border and add to trade-policy risk for markets.
whatToWatch: Which US goods face the new tariffs
Any US response to the announcement

stories.title: Carney: Canada's retaliatory tariffs on US goods start September 8
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada's retaliatory tariffs on US goods will take effect September 8. The announcement follows the collapse of trade talks with Washington, CNBC reported.
stories.whyItMatters: A firm start date gives markets a concrete deadline to price in new trade friction affecting cross-border supply chains.
whatToWatch: September 8 tariff start date
Any last-minute talks between the US and Canada before then
questions: Which goods will the tariffs cover?
How is the US likely to respond?

stories.title: Treasury announcement sparks rally in gold and bitcoin
stories.summary: An announcement from the US Treasury this week triggered a rally in both gold and bitcoin, MarketWatch reported. The report ties the gains in both assets to the same piece of policy news.
stories.whyItMatters: Gold and bitcoin often rally together when investors seek safe havens, so a shared driver points to a shift in sentiment on fiscal or dollar policy.

Whether gold and bitcoin hold their gains
